status_semantics.release_qualified: Current method-factory evidence proves the bounded method, archive, native workflow, export, method-audit, and packaged Windows acceptance tiers.
status_semantics.native_qualified: Current method-factory evidence proves engine, archive, native setup/results, and export tiers, but not packaged release qualification.
status_semantics.absent: No promotion evidence is admitted. Typed configuration, a preview payload, fit fields, documentation, or a future contract does not count as implementation.
status_semantics.audit_passed: The support boundary and blockers were reproduced from current source bytes. It does not mean Phase 5 is complete.

source_probes.contains: CB-SEM/CFA ML v1 is validated for the documented QuickPLS v1.2.4 raw-data single-group reflective ML scope

blockers: The release-qualified baseline does not promote bootstrap, invariance, multigroup, model comparison, moderator, robust ML, ordinal WLSMV, FIML, or general equality-constraint tracks.
The supported claim remains bounded to continuous reflective single-group raw-data ordinary ML.
The v2 full-refit candidate has no completed B=1000 through 10000 qualification simulation or accepted method-factory evidence, so the manifest remains absent.

Archive validation recomputes identities, indexed sample-position digests, accounting, warnings, and Type-7 summaries from stored witnesses, but it does not replay every ML fit; coordinated witness and derived-summary rewrites are not authenticated and remain a promotion blocker.
No genuine packaged Windows acceptance or independent release audit exists, and the analytical cbsem_bootstrap_v1 preview remains permanently ineligible for v2 evidence.

source_probes.contains: let chi = fit.chi_square + index as f64 * groups.len() as f64;

blockers: The v1 invariance steps arithmetically alter pooled-fit statistics and do not fit configural, metric, or scalar constrained group models.
The current validated CB-SEM recipe blocks group and invariance metadata.
No identified scalar mean structure, named constraint/release ledger, hierarchy recovery simulation, strict archive, or native workflow exists.
The v1 group summaries apportion one pooled fit by group size instead of fitting group-specific and equality-constrained ML models.
No qualified metric-invariance prerequisite, target-path equality likelihood-ratio test, stratified bootstrap, group failure policy, or v2 persistence/native workflow exists.
The v1 preview is permanently ineligible for v2 promotion evidence.
Individual CB-SEM results expose AIC and BIC, but no typed two-model comparison recipe or comparison result exists.
No shared-row/data identity check, mechanical nesting validator, constrained refit, likelihood-ratio result, comparison archive, UI/export, or packaged workflow exists.
Subtracting displayed fit fields manually is not method implementation or promotion evidence.

source_probes.contains: CB-SEM ML v1 does not support interactions or higher-order constructs

blockers: The current validated CB-SEM engine and recipe validation reject interactions.
PLS two-stage moderation and PROCESS OLS moderation are different estimators and cannot evidence CB-SEM LMS moderation.
No LMS raw-data likelihood, quadrature/mixture diagnostics, simple-slope covariance, bootstrap refits, persistence, native workflow, or packaged acceptance exists.
A typed RobustMl selection exists, but validated recipe rules reject every estimator other than ordinary ML.
No sandwich/scaled statistic implementation, robust difference test, independent numerical reference, nonnormal simulation, archive identity, native workflow, or method manifest exists.
An enum value is configuration scaffolding, not engine support.
A typed Wlsmv selection exists, but validated recipe rules reject it and the engine contains no ordinal threshold or polychoric-correlation estimator.
No category coding contract, thresholds, weight matrix, mean/variance correction, sparse-cell failure policy, independent reference, simulation, archive, native workflow, or method manifest exists.
Treating ordinal codes as continuous ML data is outside this capability.
The typed missing-data policy exposes only listwise deletion and the validated CB-SEM rule requires it.
No case-pattern likelihood, missingness diagnostics, auxiliary-variable policy, independent reference, MAR simulation, archive, native workflow, or method manifest exists.
Mean imputation or listwise deletion cannot be relabeled as FIML.
The CB-SEM recipe has no general fixed/equality constraint objects, labels, bounds, or release ledger.
The optimizer parameter plan treats supported parameters as individually free or marker-fixed and has no equality mapping across free parameters.
Invariance-step names and synthetic v1 deltas are not a general constrained optimizer; no independent reference, simulation, persistence, native workflow, or method manifest exists.
